kaps_punt: Rotstekeninge - Waar, wanneer, hoe en hoekom dit geskep is | Interpretasies van rotskuns | Suid-Afrikaanse Landswapen en die Linton Rotskunspaneel

items.bewering: Op baie rotse in Suider-Afrika is daar prente wat die San lank gelede gemaak het. Ons noem hierdie prente rotskuns.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage List, Maloti-Drakensberg Park (whc.unesco.org/en/list/985): rock paintings made by the San over about 4 000 years; Wits Rock Art Research Institute pages on southern African rock art.

items.bewering: Prente wat met verf op 'n rots aangebring is, noem ons rotsskilderye. Prente wat met 'n harde klip in die rots self gekrap of gekap is, noem ons rotsgravures.
items.bron: Rozenberg Quarterly, 'Rock Art Research in South Africa' (citing Morris 1998): engravers removed the rock crust with another hard stone, by fine-line, scraped and pecked techniques; Wits Origins Centre engraving archive (Google Arts & Culture): pecking by hammering and chipping the rock surface.

items.bewering: Jy sal ook die woord rotstekeninge hoor, wat nog 'n naam vir rotskuns is.
items.bron: Afrikaans academic usage: 'rotstekeninge' used for San rock art generally in Historia (UP) and UFS/NWU repository articles found in search; the CAPS heading itself uses 'Rotstekeninge' for the whole topic.

items.bewering: Die San het op rotswande en in rotsskuilings geskilder. 'n Rotsskuiling is 'n vlak grot of 'n rotsoorhang waar mense kon skuil.
items.bron: Hall et al. 2007, South African Journal of Science (via repository.up.ac.za 2263/5766): about 30 000 painted images in nearly 600 rock shelters in the Drakensberg; Wits RARI site record Linton I: a 'long, low and moderately deep shelter'.

items.bewering: Die rots daarbo het die verf teen reën beskerm.
items.bron: UP repository, 'Deterioration of San rock art: new findings, new challenges' and Hall et al. 2007: paintings survive in rock shelters, which shelter but do not fully protect them from weathering. The claim is about rain under an overhang and does not say the paint is safe from all weathering, so it holds.

items.bewering: Rotsgravures is dikwels op groot klippe in die oop veld gemaak.
items.bron: Rozenberg Quarterly, 'Rock Art Research in South Africa': engravings sit mostly on the interior plateau, on boulders on hills or near rivers; in their original setting 'on a small hill or in an open grassland'; Northern Cape engravings mostly on dolerite boulders.

items.bewering: Twee bekende plekke met baie rotsskilderye is die Drakensberge in KwaZulu-Natal en die Cederberg in die Wes-Kaap.
items.bron: UNESCO, Maloti-Drakensberg Park (South African part, uKhahlamba-Drakensberg, KwaZulu-Natal): 'the largest and most concentrated group of rock paintings in Africa south of the Sahara'; Cederberg (Western Cape) rock art: Sevilla Rock Art Trail near Clanwilliam, run with the South African Museum, nine painted sites (portfoliocollection.com; southafrica.net Clanwilliam Living Landscape Project).

items.bewering: Rotskuns is nie in een jaar of selfs in een eeu gemaak nie. Mense het geslag ná geslag oor 'n baie lang tyd prente op die rotse gemaak.
items.bron: UNESCO, Maloti-Drakensberg Park: rock paintings made by the San 'over a period of 4 000 years'.

items.bewering: Op party rotswande is nuwer prente bo-oor ouer prente geskilder.
items.bron: PBS Nature, 'San rock art of the Drakensberg': many rock faces carry several layers of superimposed paintings; Bradshaw Foundation (Maggs & Mazel): Mazel used newer images painted over older ones to build a relative chronology.

items.bewering: Sommige rotskuns is duisende jare oud.
items.bron: Wits / Oxford / Laval study 2017 (EurekAlert, Live Science): paintings in Lesotho and the Eastern Cape Drakensberg dated to as far back as about 3 000 years, in south-eastern Botswana to at least 5 500 years.

items.bewering: Die San het hulle verf self van kleurstowwe uit die natuur gemaak. Oker is 'n rooi, geel of bruin grondsoort wat hulle fyn gemaal het.
items.bron: Prinsloo et al. 2013, University of Pretoria repository (2263/42485): red and yellow ochres are iron-rich clays that are ground to a fine powder to make a durable paint base.

items.bewering: Houtskool uit 'n vuur het 'n swart kleur gegee.
items.bron: Prinsloo et al. 2013 (UP repository) and related pigment studies: in San rock art only carbonaceous black (charcoal or soot) has so far been detected, not manganese.

items.bewering: Die droë poeier alleen sou nie goed aan die rots vassit nie. Daarom het hulle dit met 'n bindmiddel gemeng, sodat die verf aan die rots vasklou.
items.bron: Prinsloo et al. 2013 (UP repository); Arocena et al. 2008, Geoarchaeology: binding agents in San paint include fat, egg, blood and plant resin or sap.

items.bewering: 'n Rotsgravure het geen verf nodig gehad nie. Die kunstenaar het die buitenste laag van die rots weggekrap, en die rots daaronder was dikwels ligter van kleur.
items.bron: Rozenberg Quarterly (citing Morris 1998): the patina (rock crust) is removed with another hard stone to expose 'the lighter coloured rock beneath'; dolerite boulders carry a dark patina.

items.bewering: Die prente wys mense, diere, jagtogte en danse.
items.bron: The Met, 'San Ethnography' essay; Cederberg trail descriptions (trance dances, hunting scenes, eland); Wits RARI Linton I record (human figures, eland, jackals).

items.bewering: Die eland, 'n groot wildsbok, verskyn veral dikwels.
items.bron: The Met, 'San Ethnography': eland were the most frequently painted animal, although the San mostly ate smaller antelope. A ranking claim, so recorded as a superlative; the lesson's 'veral dikwels' is, if anything, softer than the source.

items.bewering: Vroeër het baie mense gedink die prente wys net die daaglikse lewe van die San. Volgens hierdie mense het die kunstenaars net geskilder wat hulle elke dag gesien het, soos 'n jagtog.
items.bron: The Met, 'San Ethnography' ('gaze and guess', the art read as 'a sort of menu'); Bradshaw Foundation rock art network: the shamanistic framework rejected readings of the art as 'scenes of everyday life' that flourished in the early to mid twentieth century (Burkitt 1928, Breuil 1948, Willcox 1956).

items.bewering: Later het navorsers die prente vergelyk met stories wat San-mense self vertel het.
items.bron: The Met, 'San Ethnography': the Bleek and Lloyd /Xam records of the 1870s (about 12 000 pages, held at UCT) let scholars connect the art to San belief; Archaeology Magazine (1999): studying nineteenth- and twentieth-century accounts of San beliefs from the 1970s.

items.bewering: Vandag dink talle navorsers dat baie prente met die San se geloof en die genesingsdans verband hou. Tydens hierdie dans het genesers probeer om siek mense gesond te maak.
items.bron: The Met, 'San Ethnography': the art is linked to the healing or trance dance, where healers draw on supernatural power to heal the sick among other things; Bradshaw Foundation: the religious and trance reading (Vinnicombe, Pager, Lewis-Williams) became the dominant model from the late 1970s. 'Talle navorsers' is accurate. The model has its critics (a 2018 critique), so 'talle' rather than 'alle' is right.

items.bewering: Die eland was ook in die San se geloof 'n baie belangrike dier.
items.bron: The Met, 'San Ethnography': supernatural power was believed to reside in great quantity in the eland; Vinnicombe's Drakensberg work puts the eland at the centre of San belief.

items.bewering: Albei verklarings is interpretasies, en nie een van hulle is die finale antwoord nie. Die kunstenaars leef lankal nie meer nie, en ons kan hulle nie vra wat hulle bedoel het nie.
items.bron: Bradshaw Foundation and The Met: the meaning of individual images remains debated, and the religious model is itself criticised. The painting tradition ended in the nineteenth century. Both statements are literally true. Note for the writer: specialists today largely reject the 'only daily life' reading, which the lesson already marks with 'Vroeër' and 'talle navorsers', so the two readings are not presented as equal. Do not make the closing sentence any more even-handed than it is.

items.bewering: Die Linton-paneel is 'n bekende rotsskildery uit die Oos-Kaap. Dit was eers deel van die wand van 'n rotsskuiling.
items.bron: Wits RARI site record 'Linton I' (rari.wits.ac.za): rock shelter RSA LIN1 near Maclear, Eastern Cape; Iziko archaeology collection page: found in a rock shelter in the Eastern Cape; a Wits dissertation calls it one of the most viewed pieces of rock art in South Africa.

items.bewering: Meer as honderd jaar gelede is die stuk rots met die skildery uitgehaal en na Kaapstad geneem.
items.bron: Wits RARI 'Linton I': removed between 1916 and 1918, through G.S.T. Mandy, for Louis Péringuey, director of the South African Museum in Cape Town (sources give 1917 or 1918). In 2026 that is 108 to 110 years ago.

items.bewering: Vandag is dit in die Iziko Suid-Afrikaanse Museum (South African Museum) in Kaapstad.
items.bron: Wits RARI 'Linton I': 'currently housed in the South African Museum, Cape Town, where they are on public display'; Iziko archaeology collection page (iziko.org.za/collection/archaeology); Wits/The Conversation 2022: displayed at Iziko South African Museum.

items.bewering: Die paneel wys onder meer mensfigure in fyn besonderhede.
items.bron: Wits RARI 'Linton I': the panel is 'exceptionally well-preserved and detailed', with 'detailed human figures', therianthropes, eland and other images.

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika het in 2000 'n nuwe landswapen gekry.
items.bron: gov.za, 'National Coat of Arms': launched on Freedom Day, 27 April 2000.

items.bewering: Op die skild van die landswapen staan twee mensfigure wat na mekaar kyk.
items.bron: gov.za, 'National Coat of Arms': the shield 'contains two human figures from Khoisan rock art', 'depicted facing one another in greeting and in unity'.

items.bewering: Die twee figure is gebaseer op mensfigure van die Linton-paneel.
items.bron: Wits University / The Conversation, 'Rock art: how South Africa's coat of arms got to feature an ancient San painting' (2022), interviewing Sam Challis, head of the Wits Rock Art Research Institute, which the government consulted on the design: 'The two human figures come from one painting of a male figure ... He's been mirrored and stylised to form a gesture of greeting.' gov.za and Wikipedia say only that the figures are 'derived from images on the Linton stone' and do not settle the count, so the specialist source decides it.
items.regstelling: Both figures come from ONE human figure on the Linton panel, mirrored so that the two face each other. Say that, or narrow it to the two figures being based on a human figure from the Linton panel. Do not say they are based on several figures. Keep 'twee mensfigure wat na mekaar kyk' in the sentence before; that is correct.

items.bewering: Die leuse onderaan is in /Xam geskryf, 'n San-taal wat nie meer gepraat word nie.
items.bron: gov.za: motto in 'the Khoisan language of the /Xam people'; STIAS (Stellenbosch Institute for Advanced Study), 'Rediscovering a Khoisan language': /Xam is 'now extinct', once spoken by San communities in the Cape and interior; Wikipedia /Xam language: last speakers died in the 1910s; Wits/The Conversation 2022: no longer spoken.

items.bewering: Dit beteken min of meer: verskillende mense verenig.
items.bron: gov.za: literally 'diverse people unite'; Wits/The Conversation 2022: 'diverse people, unite'.

items.bewering: So eer die landswapen San-kuns as deel van 'n erfenis wat alle Suid-Afrikaners gemeen het.
items.bron: gov.za, 'National Coat of Arms': San rock art figures and a /Xam motto chosen as symbols of unity and a shared identity for the nation. An interpretive sentence consistent with the official description.

items.bewering: Rotskuns is deel van Suid-Afrika se erfenis. Dit is ook 'n bron waaruit ons oor die San se lewe en geloof leer.
items.bron: National Heritage Resources Act 25 of 1999, s 2 ('archaeological' includes rock art); The Met, 'San Ethnography' (the art as evidence of San belief).

items.bewering: 'n Beskadigde prent kan nooit weer net so gemaak word nie.
items.bron: National Heritage Resources Act 25 of 1999, preamble: 'Our heritage is unique and precious and it cannot be renewed'; RARI and SAHRA: the original artists' tradition has ended.

items.bewering: Daarom beskerm die wet rotskuns vandag, en niemand mag dit beskadig nie.
items.bron: National Heritage Resources Act 25 of 1999, s 2: 'archaeological' includes 'rock art, being any form of painting, engraving or other graphic representation on a fixed rock surface or loose rock or stone ... older than 100 years, including any area within 10m'; s 35: no one may damage or otherwise disturb such a site without a permit from the heritage authority (SAHRA permit practice, sahris.sahra.org.za). The permit exception is for research and removal, not damage, so the lesson's plain form is fair for Grade 5.

items.bewering: Besoekers moet nie daaraan raak of daarop skryf nie.
items.bron: Afrikaans heritage sources found in search (landowners asked to stop rock art being wetted or scratched, damage punishable); PBS Nature and Hall et al. 2007 on vandalism as a cause of deterioration. Standard conservation guidance.

items.bewering: Kaart: die Drakensberge in KwaZulu-Natal en die Cederberg in die Wes-Kaap; die Oos-Kaap, waar die Linton-paneel vandaan kom, en Kaapstad, waar dit vandag in die museum is; die paneel se verskuiwing van die Oos-Kaap na Kaapstad.
items.bron: Same sources as the study blocks: UNESCO Maloti-Drakensberg; Sevilla trail (Cederberg); Wits RARI 'Linton I' (near Maclear, Eastern Cape, removed to the South African Museum, Cape Town).

items.bewering: rotskuns: Kuns wat mense op klip verf of in die klip inkap.
items.bron: National Heritage Resources Act 25 of 1999, s 2(b): rock art is 'any form of painting, engraving or other graphic representation on a fixed rock surface or loose rock or stone, which was executed by human agency'.

items.bewering: rotsskildery: 'n Prent wat met verf op 'n rots geskilder is. rotsgravure: 'n Prent wat in die rots self gekrap of gekap is.
items.bron: Rozenberg Quarterly (Morris 1998): engraving by scraping or pecking away the rock crust; Prinsloo et al. 2013 (UP): painted pigments on rock.

items.bewering: rotsskuiling: 'n Vlak grot of rotsoorhang waar mense kon skuil.
items.bron: Wits RARI 'Linton I' shelter description (long, low, up to 2 m deep); Hall et al. 2007 (shelters as the main painted sites).

items.bewering: oker: 'n Rooi, geel of bruin grondsoort waarvan mense verf gemaak het. kleurstof: Iets wat kleur gee, soos oker of houtskool in verf.
items.bron: Prinsloo et al. 2013 (UP repository): ochres are iron-rich clays (red, yellow; brown shades from iron oxides); black from carbonaceous material.

items.bewering: bindmiddel: Iets wat met kleurpoeier gemeng word sodat die verf vasklou.
items.bron: Prinsloo et al. 2013 and Arocena et al. 2008: binding agents (fat, egg, blood, plant resin) mixed with pigment.

items.bewering: genesingsdans: 'n Dans van die San waarin genesers siek mense probeer gesond maak.
items.bron: The Met, 'San Ethnography': the healing or trance dance, at which healers or shamans heal the sick.

items.bewering: landswapen: 'n Land se amptelike teken, met prente en 'n leuse. leuse: 'n Kort sin wat sê waarvoor 'n land of groep staan.
items.bron: gov.za, 'National Coat of Arms': the coat of arms is the highest visual symbol of the State, made up of symbols and a motto.

items.bewering: interpretasie: 'n Verklaring van wat iets beteken, waaroor mense kan verskil. erfenis: Dinge en gewoontes wat ons uit die verlede ontvang, bewaar en aan die volgende geslagte oordra.
items.bron: National Heritage Resources Act 25 of 1999, preamble: heritage to be conserved 'so that it may be bequeathed to future generations', including tangible and intangible traditions. 'Interpretasie' is a general-language definition consistent with standard usage.

opsomming: One claim is wrong: the two figures on the coat of arms come from ONE human figure on the Linton panel, mirrored, not from several figures (Wits Rock Art Research Institute); everything else checked out. The lesson has no strict superlatives and no analogies, and the one ranking claim (the eland appears especially often) is confirmed.
